summary: Draft candidate package for AllowRemoteDASD under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\I/O System. The clean Win25H2Clean baseline confirmed the live value, the path-aware static pass found an exact current-build ntoskrnl.exe value hit, and a naturally resolved current-build Ghidra export showed that the strongest code route opens the removable-storage policy path instead of the intended Session Manager I/O path. The tools-hardened path-aware ETW lane completed shell-safe with a real I/O burst but stayed a clean no-hit for the intended path, an earlier Linux KVM Procmon replay also produced a real CSV with zero intended-path or collision hits, and KVM local-KD follow-ups first resolved `nt!IopAllowRemoteDASD` and then disassembled the live function, confirming the same removable-storage policy path plus the `AllowRemoteDASD` value literal on the running guest. A later recovery-backed KVM Procmon replay reopened the elevated guest shell automatically and still returned zero intended-path, value-name, or collision hits. That keeps the lane at Class B with runtime_no_read while removing most remaining path-context doubt around both the current-build route and the KVM runtime transport.

setting.name: Allow Remote DASD
setting.casual_explanation: Allow Remote DASD is a low-level Session Manager I/O value that appears related to raw disk access policy.
setting.why_people_change_it: Researchers track it when studying removable storage policy overlap and low-level I/O access behavior.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The lane now has baseline existence, an exact current-build value-name hit, a decisive current-build Ghidra route to a removable-storage policy path, runtime replays across ETW and multiple KVM Procmon passes that all stayed no-hit for the intended path, and KVM local-KD follow-ups that confirm both the live `IopAllowRemoteDASD` symbol and the same removable-storage policy path on the running guest.
setting.professional_notes: Phase-0 existence confirmed AllowRemoteDASD on the live Win25H2Clean baseline with preview value 0 under Session Manager I/O System. The path-aware static pass over the narrowed binary set found an exact current-build ntoskrnl.exe value hit for AllowRemoteDASD, but no exact intended path-context string in the narrowed exact-string scan. The decisive current-build Ghidra export then showed the naturally resolved ntoskrnl.exe function opening \REGISTRY\MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\RemovableStorageDevices and querying AllowRemoteDASD there. A tools-hardened path-aware ETW lane then ran both short and split I/O-burst traces against the intended Session Manager I/O path on RegProbe-Baseline-ToolsHardened-20260330. It produced real ETL/CSV outputs, kept shell health clean, and still returned a clean no-hit for both the exact value name and the intended path. A Linux KVM Procmon replay then ran a raw I/O burst, produced a real 267176-line CSV, and still returned zero lines containing the intended Session Manager I/O path, AllowRemoteDASD itself, or the removable-storage collision path. A debugger-assisted KVM local-KD follow-up then attached to the live guest kernel, resolved `nt!IopAllowRemoteDASD` directly, and returned the current-build symbol address without timing out. A deeper local-KD disassembly and string-dump follow-up on the same guest then showed `IopAllowRemoteDASD` calling `IopOpenRegistryKey` and `IopGetRegistryValue`, with its live path literal resolving to `\REGISTRY\MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\RemovableStorageDevices` and its live value-name literal resolving to `AllowRemoteDASD`. A later recovery-backed KVM Procmon replay explicitly started from a closed elevated guest shell, reopened that shell through the hardened host runner, produced a fresh 235794-line CSV, and still returned zero lines containing the intended Session Manager I/O path, the value name itself, or the removable-storage collision path. That means the strongest current-build route is no longer path-ambiguous on the working guest; the blocker is now cross-transport runtime attribution rather than uncertainty about which path the inspected function targets or whether the KVM operator state was incomplete.
